subject: Banking
title: The Bank of United States
description: A 60-second lesson on The Bank of United States.

hook.text: In 1930, the Bank of United States failed. Despite its name, it was a private bank.

buildup.text: The bank's directors had made risky real estate loans and manipulated the bank's stock price to hide losses.

discovery.text: It was the largest bank failure in American history at the time. The FDIC didn't exist yet — deposits had no protection.

twist.text: Other banks refused to rescue it because its customers were mostly Jewish immigrants.

climax.text: The failure deepened the Great Depression in New York. Fear spread to every bank, accelerating bank runs nationwide.

punchline.text: 400,000 depositors lost everything. No FDIC. No rescue. Fear spread nationwide.

quiz.question: Why did other banks refuse to rescue the Bank of United States?
options: Bias against its predominantly immigrant customers

details.summary: The Bank of United States failed in December 1930, becoming the largest US bank failure up to that time. Its misleading name made many depositors believe it was a government institution, and its collapse accelerated the Great Depression's banking panic.
details.whyItMatters: Despite its name, the Bank of United States was a private bank serving mainly immigrant communities. Its failure disproportionately affected the poor and demonstrated how bank names can mislead depositors about safety.
takeaways: The Bank of United States had over 400,000 depositors when it failed
Its name confused depositors into believing it was government-backed
The failure triggered panic withdrawals at banks across New York

faq.question: Why was the Bank of United States not saved?
faq.answer: Other New York banks considered a rescue but ultimately refused, partly due to anti-immigrant prejudice since its depositors were mainly Jewish immigrants. The failure to save it was later seen as a critical mistake that deepened the Depression.

faq.question: How did the failure accelerate the Depression?
faq.answer: The bank's official-sounding name made its failure seem like a government default to many. Panic spread rapidly, triggering runs on other banks. The cascading failures contracted the money supply and credit, deepening the economic catastrophe.
